lines.say: Berkshire invests a hundred seventy-six billion dollars that isn't its money.

lines.text: That money is called float: premiums come in now, claims get paid later.
lines.say: That money is called float: premiums come in now, claims get paid later.

lines.text: Warren Buffett, 2020 letter: "funds that do not belong to us, but are nevertheless ours to deploy."
lines.say: Buffett called it funds that do not belong to us, but are nevertheless ours to deploy.

scene.text: Funds that do not belong to us, but are nevertheless ours to deploy.

lines.text: Hypothetical: a $1,000 premium invested 5 years at an assumed 4% a year: $1,000 x 1.04^5 = $1,216.65.
lines.say: Say a thousand-dollar premium earns an assumed four percent for five years: about twelve hundred seventeen dollars.

lines.text: Even if the claim takes the full $1,000 in year 5, the insurer keeps $216.65.
lines.say: Even if the claim takes the whole thousand, the insurer keeps about two hundred seventeen.

lines.text: It began in 1967 with National Indemnity, bought for $8.6 million.
lines.say: It began in nineteen sixty-seven with National Indemnity, bought for eight point six million dollars.

lines.text: Berkshire's float: $39 million in 1970, about $176 billion at the end of 2025.
lines.say: Float grew from thirty-nine million in nineteen seventy to about one hundred seventy-six billion by twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In 2025, insurance underwriting itself earned $7.26 billion after tax, so the float cost less than nothing.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, underwriting alone earned seven point two six billion after tax, so the float cost less than nothing.

lines.text: Greg Abel became Berkshire's CEO on January 1, 2026.

post.title: Berkshire invests $176 billion that isn't its own money
post.ig:
Berkshire Hathaway invests billions that aren't its money.

It's insurance float: premiums collected now, claims paid later. Berkshire's float was about $176B at the end of 2025, up from $39M in 1970.
It began with National Indemnity, bought for $8.6M in 1967.
In 2025, insurance underwriting earned $7.26B after tax, so the float cost less than nothing.
Hypothetical: $1,000 held 5 years at an assumed 4% = $1,216.65.
Greg Abel became CEO on Jan 1, 2026.

Sources: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters (2010, 2020, 2025) and FY2025 10-K; Berkshire news release May 5, 2025.
